name: Enterprise Financial Event and Multi-Ledger Binding
holds: Chart of Accounts / Accounting Policy has no registry allocation, so the profile is non-instantiable.
Base ownership contradictions and currency/close semantics remain unresolved.
Exactly one frozen audit completed and all material defects were remediated without rerun.
No runtime ID, registry allocation or publication is allowed.

constraintRules.rule: Profile is correspondence-only and mints no subject identity, account, Chart, policy, ledger, entry, posting, balance, event, invoice or payment identity.
WM-ECO-015 exclusively owns externally serviced Financial Accounts; Ledger Account is never its subtype or profile.
The required unassigned Chart of Accounts / Accounting Policy base exclusively owns Ledger Account identity and posting eligibility; profile is non-instantiable until allocated.
WM-ECO-016 exclusively owns ledger-local Journal Entry, Posting and closed-kind correction-relation occurrence identity; profile never carries correction links.
WM-ECO-017 exclusively owns qualified immutable balance and position assertions.
External events, WM-ECO-008 invoices and WM-ECO-009 payments remain externally mastered correlation references.
Every binding pins source identity plus revision, valid time or as-of time and is append-only with supersession.
Sibling correlation sets use candidate-defined divergence-reason codes and pin the compared policy revisions; profile defines no vocabulary.
No profile relation participates in balancing, netting, plugging, tolerance or correction arithmetic.
Each entry balances inside exactly one ledger under the candidate-defined currency role, scope and tolerance rules.
Optional Financial Account backing is context- and interval-qualified, at most one per context, and never Ledger Account identity.
Correcting one sibling does not mutate, freeze or automatically correct another ledger's sibling set.
Profile cannot cascade-delete or mutate any upstream master.
A profile-local binding key is non-subject, has profile-only resolvability, and exists solely for append-only supersession; it never becomes enterprise identity.
